title: Spring All-Hands — draft intro & Q&A (Maya Chen)
body:
Purpose: rough personal notes for the Spring all-hands intro + anticipated Q&A. This is a scratchpad — not final. Use for rehearsal, drop comments, then file final copy in Confluence.

Top-level messages (3):
- We are focused on predictable inference: reliability + cost controls = customer trust. show 3 real examples (hosted API customer, dedicated partner, private deployment PoC).
- Product ops: invest in tooling that reduces unit costs (Optimize features + batching defaults). show rough % cost drop target (engineering ballpark: 10–18%). TODO confirm with Elena.
- People & pace: hiring slow-down in non-critical IC roles, ramp for infra and SRE. Be explicit about promo cycles and mentorship plan.

Opening script (30–45s):
- "Hi everyone — quick thanks for shipping through a gnarly quarter. Today we want to be blunt about where we're investing and why. We exist to make inference predictable for engineers and the companies they build. That shapes every decision you saw this quarter."
- Pause — call out a customer snippet: "We helped FinPartner reduce tail latency by 40% with Dedicated+autoscale changes" (source: Jun — validate stat).

Product highlights to call out (one slide each):
1) Hosted API: streaming improvements, function-calling reliability fixes, billing transparency dashboard (console).
2) Dedicated: reserved capacity autoscale rules & burst window announcement (alpha).
3) Private: two new KMS integrations + puppet/helm on-prem installer (pilot).
4) Optimize: batching suggestion engine + quantization recipe pilot (internal beta).

Metrics to show (rough, need final numbers):
- API p50 / p95 latency trends (last 90d) — show targets vs actual. (Finance ask: show cost per 1M tokens last quarter).
- Dedicated committed revenue and utilization: target 70% utilization on reserved pools.
- Customer NPS: overall & product-specific signal (hosted vs dedicated).

Org update bullets (sparse):
- Small reorg: infra + runtime teams to consolidate GPU scheduling work (lead: Samir). Rationale: reduce duplication, speed kernel selection improvements.
- New headcount focuses: SRE (+2), infra software (+3), product analytics (+1).
- Promotion cycles: announcing mid-April; managers to complete calibration by 4/10.

Anticipated Q&A (with scratch answers):
Q: Are we hiring?
A: Yes — selective hiring. focus = SRE & runtime. not a full freeze. (If pressed on numbers: point to hiring plan doc; trade-offs: cost vs critical delivery).

Q: What does "predictable" mean for customers?
A: predictable = latency SLOs + cost transparency + automated fallback policies. Example: route-to-compatible-model on congestion. Link to recent incident post-mortem for example (Jun).

Q: Will there be layoffs?
A: No planned layoffs. We are optimizing priorities and slowing external hiring while protecting critical roles. Be empathetic; refer to People inbox for 1:1 requests.

Q: How will this impact compensation/promotions?
A: Promo cycle still on schedule; comp budget tighter — we expect fewer out-of-cycle increases. Managers must document impact / career plan in calibration packets.

Q: Roadmap asks — where does Redwood Private rank?
A: Private remains high priority for regulated customers; plan = support GA pilots this quarter for two pilot customers, then scale. Highlight: new KMS + audit logs.

Open items / TODOs (for me & collaborators):
- [ ] Finalize numbers w/ Elena (ARR impact, cost per token). target: 3/12.
- [ ] Get customer quote from CS (FinPartner latency stat) — Jun to confirm.
- [ ] Slide deck final pass (narrative flow + 1-liner per slide) — Samir to review by 3/09.
- [ ] Prepare leaked-question doc for managers (FAQ short answers) — people-ops owns.

Logistics & rehearsal notes:
- All-hands Wed 3/18 10:00 PT, 60 mins. Script target: 12–15 mins for exec updates, 25 mins for product demos, 20 for live Q&A.
- AV: use internal room setup. mic check 9:45. Virtual: ensure captions on.
- Backup plan: if live demo fails, have recorded video + screenshot-only slides.

Tone guidance (notes to self):
- Honest but forward-looking. Avoid evasive corporate phrasing. When discussing hard trade-offs (hiring, budget), be concrete about what we will do and how employees are supported.
- Avoid deep technical detail in exec segment — highlight impact. Technical deep dives can be in breakout follow-ups.

Rough rehearsal script fragments (bullet-y, for reading):
- "We are prioritizing three things: predictable inference performance, lower unit economics for customers, and customer-grade operational tooling. Everything else gets deprioritized until those are healthy."
- "We will measure success by latency percentiles, cost per token, and customer uptime — and we will share those metrics monthly."

Risks & talking points if pressed:
- Risk: short-term slower feature cadence. Response: trade-off deliberate; focus on stability and cost reduction yields better customer retention.
- Risk: people morale. Response: invest in transparency, manager check-ins, small wins. encourage managers to host skip-levels next 2 weeks.

Appendix notes (links / refs):
- Incident postmortem: confluence://ORG/infra-incident-2026-02
- Hiring plan doc: confluence://people/hiring-plan-FY26Q2
- Billing & cost analysis (draft): github://redwood/finance/cost-analysis/branch-03

Notes for finalization:
- Make the opening anecdote shorter (10–12s).
- Replace any rough stats with verified numbers before sharing. Mark any stats with [VERIFY].
- Add brief shout-outs slide: hiring, on-call responders, infra release owners.

Random scratch ideas (keep or delete):
- Quick internal poll live during all-hands: "Which product should get investment priority?" — use Slack emoji. Might be noisy.
- Tiny customer video clip: 20s explain impact of dedicated autoscale.

—— end of scratchpad —
If anyone reads this and wants to add: please drop inline comments or copy to Confluence once we lock numbers.
